bullets.title: Applying International Medication Safety Standards
bullets.text: International healthcare systems use different charts, formularies, electronic records and controlled-drug procedures. Although local processes vary, safe practice is built on consistent identification, allergy checking, clinical assessment, documentation and communication. An IQN must learn the local system before…

bullets.title: Clinical Pharmacology and High-Risk Medicines
bullets.text: Some medicines have a greater potential to cause serious harm if used incorrectly. Internationally qualified nurses must combine pharmacological knowledge with current patient assessment, pathology results and monitoring requirements.

bullets.title: Medication Reconciliation, Communication and Incident Management
bullets.text: Medication harm often occurs when patients move between home, emergency care, hospital wards, aged care and community services. Accurate medication reconciliation and clear communication protect patients during these transitions.

bullets.title: Person-Centred Medication Education and Shared Decision-Making
bullets.text: Medication safety improves when patients understand and participate in treatment decisions. International nurses care for people with different languages, beliefs, health literacy and access to medicines. Education should be individualised without making assumptions.
